title: Mandatory mediation in civil actions
intro: This guide explains what Rule 24.1 of the Rules of Civil Procedure says about mandatory mediation in some Superior Court of Justice actions: where it applies, when the session happens, choosing a mediator, attendance, documents, and what happens afterwards.

sections.heading: What mandatory mediation is
paragraphs: Rule 24.1 “provides for mandatory mediation in specified actions, in order to reduce cost and delay in litigation and facilitate the early and fair resolution of disputes.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.01)
“In mediation, a neutral third party facilitates communication among the parties to a dispute, to assist them in reaching a mutually acceptable resolution.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.02)

In this Rule, a “defence” includes “a notice of intent to defend”, “a statement of defence”, and a notice of motion in response to an action, other than a motion challenging the court's jurisdiction. Several time limits in this Rule run from the first defence filed. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.03, 24.1.09 (1), (6))

sections.heading: Where it applies
paragraphs: The Rule applies to actions governed by it immediately before January 1, 2010, and to actions commenced on or after January 1, 2010 in “The City of Ottawa.”, “The City of Toronto.” or “The County of Essex.” It also applies to actions transferred to one of those counties on or after January 1, 2014, unless the court orders otherwise. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.04 (1))

The Rule does not apply to some actions, including “actions under Rule 64 (Mortgage Actions)”, actions on the Toronto Region Commercial List, actions under the Construction Act (except trust claims), and actions under the Bankruptcy and Insolvency Act (Canada). It does not apply to actions certified as class proceedings, and applies to an action started under the Class Proceedings Act, 1992 “only if certification as a class proceeding has been denied”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.04 (2), (2.1))
“The court may make an order on a party's motion exempting the action from this Rule.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.05)

sections.heading: When the session happens
paragraphs: “A mediation session shall take place within 180 days after the first defence has been filed, unless the court orders otherwise.” In deciding whether to extend or shorten that time, the court considers all the circumstances, including the number of parties, the state of the pleadings, the complexity of the issues, and whether a party intends to bring a summary judgment motion. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.09 (1), (2))

For an action transferred to Ottawa, Toronto or Essex on or after January 1, 2014, the 180-day time limit and the automatic assignment of a mediator after 180 days do not apply, and “the court may make an order, on motion or otherwise, specifying the date by which a mediation session must take place.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.09 (2.1))

The session “may be postponed to a later date if, (a) the parties consent to the date in writing; and (b) the consent is filed with the mediation co-ordinator.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.09 (3))

sections.heading: The mediator
paragraphs: The mediation is conducted by “a person chosen by the agreement of the parties from the list for a county”, a person assigned from the list by the mediation co-ordinator, or “a person who is not named on a list, if the parties consent.” “The parties shall choose a mediator under subrule 24.1.08 (2).” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.08 (2), 24.1.09 (4))

Before the action is set down for trial, one of the parties files with the mediation co-ordinator a notice (Form 24.1A) “stating the mediator's name and the date of the mediation session”, or a mediator's report showing the mediation has concluded. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.09 (5))

If the co-ordinator receives none of the listed documents or orders within 180 days after the first defence is filed, the co-ordinator “shall immediately assign a mediator from the list, unless the court orders otherwise.” The assigned mediator serves a notice (Form 24.1B) at least 20 days before the session, “advising that attendance is obligatory.” The date is to be “within 90 days after the appointment of the mediator, unless the court orders otherwise.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.09 (6), (7), (7.1))

sections.heading: Documents before the session
paragraphs: “At least seven days before the mediation session, every party shall prepare a statement in Form 24.1C and provide a copy to every other party and to the mediator.” The statement “shall identify the factual and legal issues in dispute and briefly set out the position and interests of the party making the statement.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.10 (1), (2))

The party making the statement “shall attach to it any documents that the party considers of central importance in the action.” “The plaintiff shall include a copy of the pleadings with the copy of the statement that is provided to the mediator.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.10 (3), (4))

sections.heading: Attendance and confidentiality
paragraphs: “The parties, and their lawyers if the parties are represented, are required to attend the mediation session unless the court orders otherwise.” A party who needs another person's approval to settle arranges “to have ready telephone access to the other person throughout the session”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.11 (1), (2))

Unless the court orders otherwise, where an insurer may be liable to satisfy all or part of a judgment in the action, or to indemnify or reimburse an insured party for money paid under it, a representative of the insurer attends, and the insured party is not required to. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.11 (1.1))
“All communications at a mediation session and the mediator's notes and records shall be deemed to be without prejudice settlement discussions.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.14)

sections.heading: When a party does not comply
paragraphs: If a session cannot practically go ahead because a party did not provide the statement of issues, or “fails to attend within the first 30 minutes of the time appointed”, the mediator cancels the session and files “a certificate of non-compliance (Form 24.1D).” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.10 (5), 24.1.12)

The co-ordinator then refers the matter to a judge or associate judge, who may convene a case conference and may, among other things, “establish a timetable for the action”, “dismiss the action, if the non-complying party is a plaintiff, or strike out the statement of defence, if that party is a defendant”, or “order a party to pay costs”. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.13 (1), (2))

sections.heading: After the mediation
paragraphs: “Within 10 days after the mediation is concluded, the mediator shall give the mediation co-ordinator and the parties a report on the mediation.” An agreement resolving some or all of the issues “shall be signed by the parties or their lawyers.” (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.15 (1), (3))

If the agreement settles the action, “the defendant shall file a notice to that effect”, within 10 days after an unconditional agreement is signed, or within 10 days after the condition of a conditional agreement is satisfied. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.15 (4))

If a party to a signed agreement does not comply with it, any other party may “make a motion to a judge for judgment in the terms of the agreement” or “continue the action as if there had been no agreement.” With the parties' consent, the court may at any stage order an additional mediation session. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1.15 (5), 24.1.16 (1))
Rule 24.1 does not set out mediators' fees, and this site does not yet have a source for them. (Rules of Civil Procedure, r. 24.1)
